subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add a supported configurable permission policy for agent-created user-facing files, and which write paths and default modes are in scope?
rationale: The request adds config surface and changes local filesystem access boundaries across core write paths, so automation should not choose the permanent policy or default permissions without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped Policy
options.body: Add a narrow tools/workspace-output permission policy with explicit exclusions for sensitive state, schema/docs, and tests across host, apply_patch, sandbox, and exec-related paths.

options.title: Use Fixed Defaults
options.body: Avoid new config surface and fix concrete writer defaults only where maintainers approve each boundary, such as media or workspace documents.

options.title: Document Host Setup
options.body: Leave runtime permissions unchanged and document ACL, Docker user/group, umask, or NAS permission setup as the supported operator workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Policy
recommendation.body: Add a narrow tools/workspace-output permission policy with explicit exclusions for sensitive state, schema/docs, and tests across host, apply_patch, sandbox, and exec-related paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history on the sandbox and filesystem-safety paths that would need the policy boundary.
